research_question: Can a bounded cheap-first operation-fit cascade reduce CPU routing latency while preserving supported-operation recall and near-domain unsupported-operation rejection?

selection_policy.candidate_confirmation_data: v5 calibration split only after candidate freeze
forbidden_for_selection: any v14 generated corpus or result
selection_policy.primary_objective: minimize mean CPU latency among candidates meeting both quality floors
selection_policy.tie_breaker: higher harmonic mean of supported-operation routed accuracy and near-domain unsupported-operation rejection

candidate_family.authority_constraint: both stages receive only already-authorized sibling operation choices and cannot add tools, endpoints, credentials, arguments, or side effects

isolation_requirements: No normalized exact-query overlap with v2-v13.
The v14 corpus must not exist before the complete cascade candidate is frozen.
The generator and frozen candidate configuration must be committed before the one-shot run starts.
A runtime seed must be recorded with the generated corpus and result artifact.
The generated corpus must not be opened, previewed, summarized, or used for any configuration change before scoring completes.
After the first completed scoring run, v14 is permanently consumed and may be used only for reporting or clearly labeled diagnostics.
